descripcion: The second conditional talks about an unreal present or future: if I had more time, I would travel more. At B1 the goal is to build the form correctly and use it in real, everyday hypotheticals about wishes and imagined situations.

filas: I could travel more if I had time.

ejemplos.texto: If I had more time, I would travel a lot more.
If she knew about it, she would say something.
What would you do if you won the lottery?

notas: Were is used instead of was with I/he/she/it in careful English: if I were you.
Would never appears inside the if-clause.
Use the second conditional for something unreal or unlikely, not a real future possibility.

contraste.es: El español usa si + imperfecto de subjuntivo y condicional simple (si tuviera tiempo, viajaría), con la misma lógica que el inglés. El error típico es poner would también en la cláusula con if, por analogía con would have known en español.

errores: Using would in the if-clause: if I would have time.
Using was instead of were in formal writing.
Confusing this with the first conditional for a real possibility.
autochequeo: Is the if-clause in the past simple, with no would?
Is were used instead of was in careful writing?
Is the situation genuinely unreal, not a real future possibility?
Have I used at least two full second-conditional sentences?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the second conditional. Check for would inside the if-clause, check were versus was, and check whether the situation is genuinely unreal. Do not rewrite the text.
